premises.text: Plastics are economically essential but produce massive persistent waste that recycling and industrial-compost compostables fail to solve well
premises.evidence_span: Plastics are a critical part of our modern economy. They are an enabling technology in just about every single thing that you and I all love to use

premises.text: Recycling is fragmented, laborious, and low-margin, and compostable plastics need scarce industrial compost and degrade slowly
premises.evidence_span: Recycling is great when it works, but it's fragmented, complex, it's laborious, the margins are low, it's a hard sell. So we made compostable plastics. Well, that's great, right? Well, sort of. Yeah, they break down, but you need industrial compost to do that, and those pieces of infrastructure are not all that available

premises.text: Proprietary coating stabilizes enzymes so they can be packaged inside plastics and triggered to degrade the material from the inside out
premises.evidence_span: We take enzymes and wrap them in our special proprietary coating that acts like PPE and enables us to take these fragile molecules and put them inside the plastics, where they can be triggered to degrade the materials from the inside out

premises.text: Enzyme-embedded plastics return to soil, can break down in warm water baths enabling decentralized waste streams, and support chemical recycling in industrial settings
premises.evidence_span: they completely return to the soil at the end of life. We can also break them down and warm water baths

premises.text: End-to-end engineered degradation stops microplastics at the source
premises.evidence_span: we're able to degrade from one end to the other through some clever engineering work that we were able to do, which means we stop microplastics at the source

premises.text: Drop-in additive is scalable, uses little enzyme, and degrades on demand only with water and heat
premises.evidence_span: We're developing a drop-in additive that's readily scalable. Enzymes are incredibly efficient, so we only need to use a little bit, and the degradation is on demand. It requires water and heat

premises.text: Launch focus is PLA compostable plastics to expand compostable design space, ease regulatory burdens, and widen favorable end-of-life conditions
premises.evidence_span: We're starting with PLA, which is the first compostable plastic. It's a $3.5 billion market, and it's one of the fastest growing segments within the industry. And we've chosen this because it opens up a couple of interesting avenues
